03 / PROJECTS

Selected projects.

Each project is a different way to learn by doing.

01 / FEATURED · CPU SCHEDULER

CPU scheduling, made visible.

A handheld ESP32 device that teaches operating-system scheduling. Pick an algorithm on the OLED, enter processes with four buttons, and watch the IPS screen step through every decision.

  • C++
  • ESP32
  • Embedded UI
Challenge
Turn an abstract operating-systems topic into something you can hold and step through.
Hardware
ESP32, an SSD1306 OLED for menus and input, a 240×240 ST7789 IPS display for the visualization, and four buttons.
Outcome
FCFS, SJF, SRTF, Priority, and Round Robin with step-by-step playback, a live Gantt chart, waiting, turnaround, and response times, CPU utilization, and a Compare All mode.
Source
CPU Scheduler repository

03 / PAGLA GHORA LFR

LFR: sensing, steering, and speed.

Line-following robots taught me that clean sensing, precise control, and rapid iteration matter when every millisecond changes the route.

  • Line following
  • Firmware
  • Control systems
My contribution
Physical modifications, software changes, and firmware updates through several iterations of the Mark-X and Head Hunter builds.
Mark-X firmware
PD control over a 16-sensor array read through an analog multiplexer, with a state machine that handles gaps, priority turns at junctions, inverted white-on-black sections, and an automatic stop in the finish box.
Head Hunter
An ESP32, a 14-channel reflectance sensor array, geared motors, and an OLED interface.

  • ESP32
  • Wireless

Wireless signal analyzer
An ESP32-based analyzer with an ST7789 display for exploring Wi-Fi channel analysis and Bluetooth scanning.
ESP32 smart clock
